prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: hit while turning left in Conroe, Texas. Injury: knee injury. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1085; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just go by the placeholder for today, if that's allowed. [Plaintiff Name]

Q: That's fine for the transcript. Where do you currently live?

A: In the Conroe area, in a house with my spouse and our two kids.

Q: Let's talk about the accident. Where were you driving when it happened?

A: I was on a busy road in Conroe, heading to my office. I needed to make a left turn into a shopping center parking lot.

Q: What did you see before you started your turn?

A: I checked for oncoming traffic. There was a gap, so I started to turn. I remember seeing headlights coming toward me, but they seemed far enough away.

Q: Then what happened?

A: The other car came through faster than I expected. It hit the front passenger side of my car. My car spun a little and the airbag deployed. My knee hit the dashboard hard.

Q: Did you feel pain right away?

A: Yes, my right knee was throbbing almost immediately. I could hardly bend it, and I felt a lot of pressure on the joint.

Q: How did you get to the hospital or urgent care?

A: My neighbor drove me to an urgent care clinic that afternoon. They took X-rays and told me to see an orthopedic doctor.

Q: Did you follow up with that orthopedic doctor?

A: Yes. I went for an MRI, and the doctor said I had a torn meniscus. I had a few sessions of physical therapy, twice a week for a while, and I was given a brace to wear.

Q: How has the knee affected your daily life since the accident?

A: It's been hard. Stairs are the worst. I used to run a few mornings a week, and I've stopped completely. I had to change how I do the grocery shopping because standing in one spot for long stretches makes it ache.

Q: Have you missed any work?

A: I missed a number of days in the weeks right after the accident. Since then I've been working from a desk more, which helps, but I still have to get up and move around every hour or so.

Q: Do you still have pain today?

A: Yes, especially when the weather changes or after I've been on my feet too long. Some nights I wake up because the knee is stiff.

Q: Have you had any prior injuries to that same knee?

A: No, not that I can recall. I'd never had any trouble with it before this accident.
